correctness.rationale: This PASS applies only to the corrected files. The frozen definition made p the literal probability of keeping a label, so the two-card sign mean is p (the only odd outcome is the binary word 10, of probability (1−p)/2). The frozen formula gives (1+p)/2, even giving 1/2 instead of zero at p=0. Its proof and checker instead use the adhesion transition law. The repair keeps the literal convention and updates all affected formulas and checks. Its four signed states give a transfer with characteristic polynomial λ^4−2p²λ²+(2p−1)², verified by direct determinant expansion, and the displayed first four means. Independent flips with probability q=1−p yield m one-switch odd configurations (including the initial-bit choice) on an even deck; on an odd deck one switch has even sign and both initial bits give odd sign precisely for the m(m+1)/2 pairs (odd first switch position, even second position). Thus 1−ρ has leading term mq and m(m+1)q² respectively. Character multiplication yields the time limits. Near p=1 the two subsequence roots are p²±(1−p)√(p²+2p−1); their first-order slopes are 2∓√2 in q, and solving against the initial means gives the two distinct pairs of limiting weights. Iteration indices are n/2+O(1), giving the displayed e^(−aξ), e^(−bξ) profiles including ξ=0. The recurrence itself covers all literal p, even when the roots coincide or are not real. Independent exact enumeration includes p=0 and p=1; the delivered replacement checker ran successfully (66 exact means, 42 recurrence comparisons, rare-switch counts through size 30, and growing-profile numerical error below 0.001 on the specified grid).
residual_risks: The grid is only finite numerical corroboration of the limiting profiles; the transfer and limit arguments establish the general claims. This is one sign character, not a full mixing result.

evidence: Jonasson–Morris prove O(log^4 n) total-variation mixing at fixed p in (0,1); Jiang gives fixed-deck strong-adhesion full-chain bounds. Resultary inversion records address expectation, zero-inversion probability, weak limits and cut-size dependence.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A whole-chain upper bound controls character deviations but does not give a character's exact rate or the even/odd gap. The two regimes in those mixing theorems also differ from a one-shuffle n(1−p) crossover.

checked_sources: Corrected RESULT.md, rare-switch proof and growing-deck limit; Jonasson–Morris Theorem 2.1 and Jiang's full-chain comparison
value.rationale: The alternating sign is a natural one-dimensional spectral observable and an immediate obstruction to total-variation mixing. The law isolates a real mechanism: a single rare label switch can change parity on an even deck but never on an odd one, which needs two switches. This gives genuinely different fixed-size relaxation scales and distinct nontrivial growing-deck profiles; the result is more than a correction of factors of two or a finite spectral table.
residual_risks: The sign may relax before the rest of the spectrum. No sharp total-variation profile, cutoff or joint time/size mixing claim is supported.
